name: ocpair
description: Hand a task to another OpenCode instance (for example OpenCode on the owner's Mac) and get woken when it has a final answer, needs a permission or answer, or failed — like a background subagent. # ocpair

`ocpair` drives a session on a paired OpenCode server. `ocpair ask` sends a task and blocks, without
polling the model or using your tokens, until the remote session settles. Run it with the shell's
background mode: you are woken once, when it exits, with the result in its output.

## Pair once

The owner runs `opencode pair --remote --yes` on the remote machine (a plain `opencode pair` link points
at its localhost and won't work). The link works once and expires in 5 minutes. Get it into a profile
without it passing through the conversation if you can, best first:

1. Ask the owner to run `ocpair login --name mac` in their own terminal on this machine and paste the
   link there (input is hidden). You never see it.
2. If your environment can deliver a secret to you as a file outside the conversation, ask for the link
   that way, then: `ocpair login --file <file> --name mac && rm <file>`.
3. Only if neither works: accept it in chat and run `ocpair login --link <link> --name mac` immediately.
   Once redeemed it is useless. Never repeat or log it.

Then open a session:

```sh
ocpair open --dir /path/on/the/remote --name mac     # new session there; becomes current
```

`login --model M` (or `model M --default`) sets the profile's default model for every new session; without one the remote's default is
used and ocpair warns. Use `opencode/claude-opus-5-5#high` unless told otherwise. The session token is
stored in `~/.config/ocpair/<name>.json` (0600). Never print or copy it.

`open` prints how the remote's owner can watch the session (`cd <dir> && opencode --session <id>`);
sessions are titled `[ocpair] …`.

Use absolute **remote** directories, not `~`. To drive several sessions through one login, create them with `open --alias build` / `open --alias docs` and pass `--session build` / `--session docs` (or the ID) on later commands. Named opens leave the profile's current session alone. `ocpair use <id> --alias build --name mac` names an existing session. No credentials need copying.

## Run a command (no model)

```sh
ocpair run "git status --short && cargo build" --name mac    # prints output, exits with its code
```

Use `run` for anything deterministic (clone, git, builds, tests): faster, free, and it can't drift.
Its output is also handed to the model with the next `ask`.

Above 16 KiB, `run` prints the first and last 8 KiB and gives a retained-output handle. Read the missing part, don't rerun: `ocpair page HANDLE --name mac --cursor 8192 --limit 4096`. Use the next **byte** cursor, not the decoded string length. Handles can expire.

`ocpair upload LOCAL REMOTE` / `ocpair download REMOTE LOCAL` copy binary files in the selected session's directory and verify byte count and SHA-256. Upload overwrites in one binary request (not resumable); download uses ranges and replaces the local file only after verification. No shell or agent needed on the target.

From Code Mode, call `tools.ocpair.run({ profile, session, command, background: true })`. `upload` and `download` take `{ profile, session, local, remote, background: true }`. After the acknowledgement, **do not poll**: the calling session receives a notice. Use `tools.ocpair.page({ profile, handle, cursor, limit })` for retained text.

## Hand off a task

```sh
ocpair ask "run the test suite and summarize failures" --name mac --stall 600    # shell background mode
```

`ask` refuses a busy session (pass `--queue` to queue behind it). If the caller died mid-`ask`, run the
same `ask` again: it reuses the prompt's id and resends nothing if it already arrived. `--attach FILE`
(repeatable) sends a local file inline.

The exit code and first output line say what happened:

| exit | output | next step |
| ---- | ------ | --------- |
| 0 | `DONE` + the remote's final answer + cost/tokens | use the answer |
| 2 | `PERMISSION <id> …` or `FORM <id> …` + reply command | `ocpair perm <id> once\|always\|reject` or `ocpair answer <id> '{"key": value}'`, then `ocpair wait` (background) |
| 3 | `FAILED: …` or `INTERRUPTED` + last answer | report or retry |
| 4 | `TIMEOUT` + what the session is doing (only with `--timeout SEC`) | `ocpair wait` again or `ocpair interrupt` |
| 5 | `STALLED` + what the session is doing (no activity for `--stall SEC`) | look, then `ocpair interrupt` and re-ask with exact commands |

Decide permissions yourself only when the owner's request already covers them; otherwise ask the owner.
Follow-up tasks go to the same session with another `ask`; `--new` opens a fresh session first.
Keep instructions narrow and give exact commands: a vague prompt can drift.

## Other commands

- `ocpair progress` — busy or not, recent tool calls, seconds since the last activity
- `ocpair last [--n N]` — the last completed answers (says `BUSY` first if it's still working)
- `ocpair diff [--stat]` — what the session changed on the remote
- `ocpair model <provider/id#variant> [--default]` — switch the current session's model; `--default` also for new sessions
- `ocpair status` — server, current session, busy or not, pending requests
- `ocpair interrupt` — stop the remote's current work
- `ocpair sessions [--busy] [--limit N]` — list all directories; busy means foreground execution, not parked inbox items. Code Mode: `tools.ocpair.sessions({ profile, busy: true })`.
- `ocpair stop ID1 ID2` — interrupt only the listed sessions and cancel their entire pending inbox. Check each result: this is not atomic and does not kill detached jobs. Code Mode: `tools.ocpair.stop({ profile, sessions: [id1, id2] })`.
- `ocpair use <id-or-alias>` — switch the current session
- `ocpair login --url URL --password-file PATH` — use a server URL and password instead of a link

All commands take `--name NAME` (default `default`) and `--session ID`. A rejected token or an unreachable
tunnel says to re-pair.

# ocpair

Hand tasks to another OpenCode server, for example OpenCode on your Mac, and get woken when they're done:
a background subagent on another machine.

## OpenCode

Give this to your agent:

> Install the ocpair plugin with `opencode plugin add @kommander/ocpair`. Then ask me to run
> `npx @kommander/ocpair login --name <name>` in my terminal with a link from `opencode pair --remote --yes` on the
> other machine. Never ask me for that link in chat. Use `tools.ocpair.*` to hand work to that machine, and
> ask me before approving a permission it asks for.

## Any other agent

Give this to your agent:

> Install ocpair with `npm i -g @kommander/ocpair` and copy its skill:
> `mkdir -p <your skills directory>/ocpair && cp "$(npm root -g)/@kommander/ocpair/SKILL.md" <your skills directory>/ocpair/`,
> then read it. Ask me to run `ocpair login --name <name>` in my terminal with a link from
> `opencode pair --remote --yes` on the other machine. Never ask me for that link in chat. Ask me before
> approving a permission it asks for.

## Pairing

On the other machine, `opencode pair --remote --yes` prints a link that works once, for 5 minutes. Redeem
it in your own terminal, so the agent never sees it:

```sh
npx @kommander/ocpair login --name mac    # paste the link; input is hidden
```

## Plugin

The tools are under `tools.ocpair` in Code Mode. `ask`, and `run`, `upload` or `download` with
`background: true`, return at once; the result arrives in the session as a notice. A pending `ask`
survives an OpenCode restart and reports once the project is open again; background jobs don't.

Every tool except `status` and `sessions` checks the permission action `ocpair` (resource: the profile
name), which OpenCode allows unless you say otherwise:

```jsonc
{ "permissions": [{ "action": "ocpair", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }] } // or "deny"
```

## CLI

Runs on Node 22+ or Bun (`bunx ocpair`). `ocpair` on its own lists every command; `SKILL.md` explains how
to use them.

```sh
ocpair open --dir /Users/me/code/app --name mac
ocpair run "git status --short" --name mac
ocpair ask "run the tests, summarize failures" --name mac
```

## Development

```sh
bun install
bun run typecheck && bun test && bun run build
```

To try the plugin, add this checkout's absolute path to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.

## Release

Bump `version` in `package.json`, merge, and push a matching tag (`git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0`).
The publish workflow puts it on npm.
